description:
## Problem
A one-slot lock cannot see memory held outside BenchBox: resident Apple `container` VMs, hand-started JVMs, IDEs. UAT's per-cell `_free_memory_abort_reason` (`tests/uat/phases/execute.py:1122-1198`) is not reusable from product code. Swap percentage misleads on macOS (78-85% used while pressure level is normal).

## Change
1. Host-pressure reader in `benchbox/utils/resource_limits.py`: on macOS `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level`, `kern.memorystatus_level`, psutil available memory; VM inventory from `container list --format json` / `container machine list --format json` when the CLI exists (names and configured memory, parsed from the JSON/`inspect` byte fields directly, never via `docker_assets.parse_memory_bytes`); free space on the boot volume and the benchmark output root. Non-macOS: psutil available memory and disk.
2. Admission: admit when pressure level is normal (1), `memorystatus_level` >= floor, available memory >= need, and free disk >= floor on each root. VM reservations are reported, itemized, but not subtracted: resident VM pages are already missing from available memory, and subtracting reservations would double-count and charge a job for its own stack.
3. Settings (env, documented): `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT_MIN_GIB` (need; default set by G3), `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_MIN_LEVEL` (default 35), `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_MIN_FREE_DISK_GIB` (default 50), and the shared watchdog budget resolver `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_MEMORY_BUDGET_GIB` (default 50% of physical RAM) defined here for later items.
4. If a reading fails, re-sample every 5 s for up to 30 s before refusing (memory from a just-released holder may not be reclaimed yet).
5. `benchbox.utils.host_lock` integration: an acquirer can request admission; it runs after the lock is obtained and before work; refusal releases the lock and exits non-zero with an itemized report. `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force` admits with a loud stderr warning.
6. `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock admit [--need-gib N]` for callers that hold no lock (compose bring-up).
7. If `read_memory_snapshot` / `free_space_gib` in `tests/uat/preflight_budget.py` duplicate the new readers, move them and migrate UAT imports (clean cutover).

## Decision gates
- D1 (resolved): signals are pressure level, memorystatus_level, available memory, disk. Swap is reported, never gates.
- D2 (resolved): the budget resolver (50% of RAM) lives here; the watchdog reuses it.
- G1 (stop condition): if `container` JSON lacks memory fields, record the observed schema and use `container machine inspect`; never guess.
- G2 (coordination): open critical item `uat-docker-memory-admission-decimal-units-20261030` owns `docker_assets.parse_memory_bytes` (docker_assets.py:76) and `managed_runtime.py:38`. Do not edit those; do not change `execute.py` admission semantics.
- G3 (stop condition): run `admit` on this Mac in its normal working state (agents running, `benchbox-agent` up). Choose the default need so that state admits while the incident state (available < 1 GiB, pressure >= 2) refuses. If no default satisfies both, record readings and stop for an owner decision.

## Guardrails (all heavy-guard items)
- Linked worktree from `origin/develop` via `make worktree-create`; never the primary clone; stage paths explicitly; never `git add -A`.
- `[COMMENT-POLICY-001]`: no comments or docstrings in new code. Durations use `benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()`/`elapsed_seconds()`.
- Tests use `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR` under `tmp_path` and injected readings; never touch the real `~/.benchbox/test.lock` or depend on live host pressure, VMs or disk.
- Never delete, move or recreate a lock file from code; never stop, resize or signal processes/VMs this invocation did not start.
- Keep names `test.lock`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS`, `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_SESSION_OWNER` (rename deferred on heavy-guard-status-policy).
- No automatic skip on `CI` or `BENCHBOX_EPHEMERAL_CLONE` (agent shells export `CI=true`).
- No heavy verification runs (no benchmark sweeps above scale 0.01, no real compose stacks) unless the item names one.
- External commands time out at 5 s and degrade to 'unmeasured'; unmeasured signals never refuse.

## Non-goals
The watchdog; wiring admission into entry points.
